reply.title: Squashing Values with the Logistic Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need a way to take any number from negative to positive infinity and squash it neatly into a range between zero and one. Early biometricians studying population growth noticed that growth starts slow, accelerates, and then levels off as it hits a carrying capacity. This smooth, S-shaped transition is captured by the logistic function. By adjusting the steepness parameter, we can control how abruptly the transition happens around the midpoint, turning a wide range of inputs into a reliable proportion.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic function squashes any input into a value between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness to see how the S-curve changes its slope.
reply.instructions: Change the steepness slider to see how the curve bends. Observe the output value at the fixed marker.
